channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula tem 49,3% dos votos contra 36,8% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz CNT
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential election runoff with 49.3% of voting intentions, compared to 36.8% for Flávio Bolsonaro, according to a CNT/MDA poll. The survey, with a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points and 95% confidence, also showed Lula ahead in the first round at 41.8% versus 28.2% for his opponent. Conducted between June 10–14, 2026, with 2,002 respondents nationwide, the study is registered with the TSE under BR-04256/2026.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se compara a Tom Cruise em ‘Top Gun’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) posted an AI-generated video depicting him as Tom Cruise’s Maverick in Top Gun, flying alongside his father Jair Bolsonaro and destroying boats labeled CV, PCC, and PT with machine-gun fire, symbolizing a crackdown on organized crime and the left. The video was released as a promotional tactic for an upcoming public security announcement, with Flávio claiming it will be 'bad news' for these groups. The post also includes a plug to follow the GENTE column on Instagram.

item.title: Comissão aprova moção de repúdio às declarações de Lula sobre 'traidores da pátria'
item.description: The Public Security Committee of the Chamber of Deputies approved a motion of repudiation against statements by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva regarding hanging as punishment for traitors of the homeland. The request was presented by Deputy Capitão Alden (PL-BA).

item.title: Com atuação discreta no Senado, Romário vira comentarista da Copa sem abrir mão do mandato
item.description: Senator Romário (PL-RJ) was noted as absent from Brasília by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre during a session on the 10th. Despite retaining his mandate, Romário has maintained a low profile in Congress and taken on a role as a World Cup commentator without resigning from office.

item.title: Prodesp rescinde parceria com empresa para ampliação do Muralha Paulista que está na mira do TCE
item.description: Prodesp terminated its partnership with Paladium Corp after the TCE-SP launched an investigation into alleged bidding fraud in the Muralha Paulista security program, a flagship initiative of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. The SSP stated the suspension is temporary and technical, while Prodesp denied any public expenditure related to the now-cancelled initiative.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro fala a VEJA sobre condenação pelo STF
item.description: Former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro was sentenced by the First Chamber of the STF to 4 years and 2 months in semi-open prison for attempting to interfere in the trial of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, over the coup plot. The ruling was unanimous, with rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes and ministers Cristiano Zanin, Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino in agreement. Eduardo admitted to coordinating with the U.S. government to impose sanctions on Brazilian authorities, including the 50% tariff on Brazilian goods announced by Donald Trump in July.

item.title: Eduardo diz que sentença sem respeito ao processo legal é nula
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro stated that any sentence without respect for due process is null, criticizing the STF's conviction for coercion in the course of the process. He argued that, after so many international defeats, even Minister Alexandre de Moraes knows the nullity of such decisions.

item.title: Senado aprova criação da Universidade Federal do Esporte
item.description: The Senate approved the creation of the Federal University of Sports (UFEsporte), a bill introduced by the Lula government and reported by Senator Leila Barros. The institution aims to train professionals in sports science, management, and sports medicine, emphasizing inclusion, equity, and the fight against discrimination. Academic activities are set to begin in 2027, with no immediate budgetary impact, as leadership roles will come from MEC repositioning and teaching/staff positions were already budgeted.

item.title: Mesmo irritado, Lula arrefece resistência à reunião com Alcolumbre
item.description: Despite being irritated by the situation, President Lula has softened his resistance to holding a meeting with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, following repeated appeals. The conversation, previously avoided, is now likely to take place, signaling an attempt at dialogue between the branches of government. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: "Não fui citado na forma da lei", diz Eduardo após condenação no STF
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro claims he was not properly notified according to law in the criminal case that led to his four-year-and-two-month sentence for obstructing justice. He criticizes Justice Alexandre de Moraes for failing to follow legal procedure and accuses him of being both 'victim and judge' in the case. The unanimous conviction by the STF’s First Chamber was for interfering in the trial related to the attempted coup involving his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: El Supremo de Brasil condena a Eduardo Bolsonaro por buscar ayuda de Trump para boicotear el juicio a su padre
item.description: Brazil's Supreme Federal Court unanimously convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro for seeking Donald Trump's help to pressure the court that tried his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in 2025. The ruling was issued by the same bench that convicted the former president for attempting a coup. Eduardo, residing in the U.S., is accused of instigating U.S. tariffs against Brazil to undermine his father's trial.

item.title: Dino diz que cortes de outros países descumprem reciprocidade com STF após caso Zambelli
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino stated that foreign courts violate the principle of reciprocity by denying extradition requests from Brazil, citing Italy's refusal to extradite former deputy Carla Zambelli. He argued such decisions breach international judicial cooperation agreements and undermine the effectiveness of Brazilian justice.

item.title: Comissão aprova moção de repúdio às declarações de Lula sobre ‘traidores da pátria’
item.description: The Public Security Committee of the Chamber of Deputies approved a motion of repudiation against President Lula’s statements calling Senator Flávio Bolsonaro a 'traitor of the homeland' and referencing hanging as punishment. The motion, filed by Deputy Capitão Alden (PL-BA), argues the remarks are incompatible with the presidency and contradict the 'government of love' narrative. A second motion, by Deputy Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), criticizes Lula’s comments about distrust in police stations, claiming they unjustly generalize and undermine police credibility.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação na trama golpista: entenda o que acontece agora
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro for coercion in the 2022 coup plot, sentencing him to 4 years and 2 months in semi-open regime. The unanimous decision by the First Turma bars him from running for office for up to eight years, with only clarification appeals available, which rarely change the outcome.

item.title: Livro propõe roteiro de reformas para conter a escalada autoritária no país
item.description: The book 'How to Disarm Authoritarianism in Brazil: An Agenda for Deradicalization' proposes institutional reforms in five key spheres — Communication, Education, Armed Forces and Police, Religion, and the Justice System — to counter democratic backsliding. Guided by the pillars of control, impartiality, and pluralism, the work edited by Conrado Hübner Mendes, Fernando Romani Sales, and Lucas Petroni aims to guide civil society in strengthening democracy ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: O cálculo que levou STF a condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro a 4 anos de prisão
item.description: The First Chamber of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF) unanimously convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro to 4 years and 2 months in prison, plus a fine of R$162,100, for process coercion after he attempted to interfere in his father Jair Bolsonaro’s trial via foreign sanctions and U.S.-based lobbying. The sentence was increased by two-thirds due to at least nine interference attempts, and Justice Alexandre de Moraes cited Eduardo’s financial condition as justification for the fine. Eduardo Bolsonaro was immediately declared ineligible and removed from his position as a Federal Police clerk.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que julgamento do STF é 'sem pé nem cabeça' e visa tirá-lo das eleições
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro claimed the STF's judgment against him violated due process, calling it 'without head or tail' and asserting it aims to bar him from running in the 2026 elections. He stated the decision is politically motivated and intended to remove him from the electoral race.

item.title: 'Recebeu PIX de milhões do pai', diz Alexandre de Moraes sobre condição de Eduardo Bolsonaro para pagar multa
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro to 4 years and 2 months in semi-open regime and a fine of R$150,000 for coercion in the coup plot case, stating the defendant can pay the fine because he received millions in PIX transfers from his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The ruling was joined by Ministers Cristiano Zanin, Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino, who rejected the defense's claims of parliamentary immunity and free speech, asserting that lobbying abroad against Brazil is not protected.

item.title: Entenda o crime pelo qual Eduardo Bolsonaro foi condenado pelo STF
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro of obstruction of justice for acting from the United States to pressure STF ministers during the trial of his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The conviction was based on evidence that he used his U.S. residency as a political base to intimidate Brazilian authorities, transcending legitimate political expression. The penalty ranges from 1 to 4 years in prison, plus a fine.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro a 4 anos e 2 meses em regime semiaberto
item.description: The STF sentenced Eduardo Bolsonaro to 4 years and 2 months in semi-open regime for coercion in the judicial process against his father, Jair Bolsonaro, with a fine of R$162,100 and loss of his PF clerk position. Minister Alexandre de Moraes followed the rapporteur’s vote and did not review parliamentary mandate loss, already declared by the Chamber in December 2025 due to excessive absences.

item.title: Os motivos que fazem o Ibovespa cair 0,45% nesta terça-feira
item.description: The Ibovespa fell 0.45% on Tuesday, pressured by a 1.33% drop in Petrobras shares after Brent crude fell over 4% due to a Middle East ceasefire agreement and the anticipated reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, profit-taking in the technology sector occurred as foreign investors sold Brazilian stocks and reallocated to U.S. tech, while new polls show Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential presidential runoff, raising concerns about long-term fiscal policy. Markets await the 'Superquarta' decisions from Copom and the Fed, with expectations of a 0.25 percentage point rate cut in Brazil and steady rates in the U.S.

item.title: Lula tem “recuperação forte” em SP e cenário é favorável, diz PT
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva claims Lula has experienced a 'strong recovery' in voting intentions in São Paulo, citing a Real Time Big Data poll showing a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff (44% to 47%, with a 2-point margin of error). In the first round, Bolsonaro leads with 36% to Lula’s 31%, but Silva emphasizes an upward trend and favorable conditions due to record job creation and income recovery policies.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro condenado: direita vê 'perseguição' do STF, e governistas falam em 'vitória contra golpistas'
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court unanimously convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro to four years and two months in prison under semi-open regime, a fine of 100 minimum wages, and eight years of ineligibility, ruling he coerced judges and sought foreign sanctions against Brazil’s judiciary. Bolsonarista allies condemned the ruling as political persecution and an attack on free speech, while government supporters framed it as a victory against coup plotters.

item.title: Edinho endossa apoio a João Campos, mas não crava ida de Lula a PE
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva confirmed that Lula will support João Campos (PSB) in the Pernambuco gubernatorial race in 2026, but did not confirm whether the president will campaign in the first round, citing his government agenda as priority. He emphasized that the support does not constitute hostility toward Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD), whom Lula respects, and ruled out any possibility of Marília Campos (PT) abandoning her Senate bid in Minas Gerais to run for governor. Edinho also stated that potential alliances with Alexandre Kalil (PDT) would only be possible in a runoff, should Kalil remain a candidate.

item.title: Por unanimidade, STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação em processo sobre tentativa de golpe
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court unanimously convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro of coercion in the course of a trial related to an attempted coup d'état. The ruling was issued by the First Chamber, with favorable votes from rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes and ministers Cristiano Zanin, Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro é condenado pelo STF por coação em julgamento da tentativa de golpe
item.description: Former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro was convicted by the STF’s 1st Chamber for coercion, after using U.S. government connections to pressure Brazilian authorities—including promoting Trump-era tariffs and the Magnitsky Act against Justice Alexandre de Moraes—to interfere in criminal proceedings against former President Jair Bolsonaro. The court ruled his actions constituted an illegitimate threat to national sovereignty and judicial independence.

item.title: Condenação de Eduardo Bolsonaro no STF causa inelegibilidade e altera chapa de Tarcísio
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court's unanimous conviction of Eduardo Bolsonaro for lobbying U.S. sanctions against Brazilian authorities triggers his immediate ineligibility, forcing his replacement as first substitute on André do Prado's Senate ticket in São Paulo. Though allies anticipated the setback, the speed of the ruling surprised them, and the substitution must occur before the official campaign start, within the party convention window. Prado says he awaits a reversal and considers a new trip to the U.S. to consult with his brother, while Tarcísio de Freitas and Flávio Bolsonaro remain confirmed for the June 20 campaign launch event.

item.title: Governo retira urgência de projeto sobre 6x1 e destrava votações na Câmara dos Deputados
item.description: The federal government withdrew the constitutional urgency from its bill to reduce the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, following pressure from House Speaker Hugo Motta, who had already approved a similar PEC. The move unblocks the Chamber’s agenda, allowing votes on other proposals such as AI regulation and MEI revenue expansion. The government had retained urgency to pressure the Senate but reversed course amid fears of legislative paralysis before the recess.

item.title: Governo Lula retira urgência de projeto sobre fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Lula government withdrew the constitutional urgency from the bill ending the 6x1 work scale after negotiating with House President Hugo Motta to unblock the legislative agenda. The move followed the expiration of the 45-day urgency period on May 30, which had stalled other legislation. Motta instead prioritized a constitutional amendment (PEC) on the same issue, already approved by the House on May 27, to gain greater political prominence on a popularly supported issue.

item.title: Edinho minimiza atrito e nega que Lula esteja rompido com Alcolumbre
item.description: The national president of the PT, Edinho Silva, downplayed the tension between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, stating there is no rupture between them. He noted that divergent positions are natural in democracy and that government allies are working to ease tensions, despite Lula’s resistance over the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF and the approval of contentious bills, such as the R$ 140 billion agricultural credit line.

item.title: 1ª Turma do STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação
item.description: Brazil's Supreme Court First Chamber unanimously convicted Eduardo Bolsonaro of coercion in the course of justice for attempting to pressure U.S. authorities to impose sanctions on Brazil to influence the trial against his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the rapporteur, rejected defense claims and stated the conduct was not protected by free speech.

item.title: Vorcaro “está esperando ser solto pelo Gilmar”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for president, criticized Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes' decision to release Felipe Vorcaro and replace Henrique Vorcaro's preventive detention with house arrest. Zema implied the Vorcaro family was 'waiting to be freed by Gilmar,' suggesting judicial favoritism. The statement was made in a social media post on Tuesday, the 16th.

item.title: Após veto à carne brasileira, Lula se reúne com von der Leyen e Costa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa at the G7 summit in France to discuss the European Union’s ban on Brazilian meat, set to take effect on September 3 due to antimicrobial use in livestock. The leaders agreed to pursue solutions addressing European sanitary and phytosanitary concerns and established a mechanism between Itamaraty and the European Commission to handle issues in animal-origin and steel products. Lula also advocated for greater valuation of critical minerals in producing countries and sustained financing for emerging economies.

item.title: Ao vivo: Poder360 entrevista Ronaldo Caiado
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) is participating in a live interview with Poder360 at 5 p.m. today, June 16, 2026, in Brasília. He will discuss his preparations for the 2026 elections and the measures he intends to implement if elected president, highlighting his political trajectory and policy proposals. The interview is being conducted by journalists Guilherme Waltenberg and Mariana Aquino.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação no processo do golpe
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro was unanimously convicted by Brazil's Supreme Court (STF) for coercion in the legal process, after attempting to interfere in his father Jair Bolsonaro's trial by coordinating international sanctions with the United States. The conviction carries a potential sentence of up to four years in prison and renders him ineligible for office for eight years, despite his absence and lack of personal defense. His actions also harmed the Brazilian economy and led to sanctions against Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação em processo sobre trama golpista
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) convicted former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro of coercion in the coup plot case after he attempted to interfere in his father’s trial by lobbying the U.S. government to create instability and threaten retaliation against Brazilian justices. Justice Alexandre de Moraes dismissed claims of parliamentary immunity and free speech, stating that federal deputies cannot act against their own country abroad and that Eduardo fled justice by remaining in the U.S. The conviction was unanimous in the First Chamber of the STF, with Moraes joined by Zanin, Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino.

item.title: "Ação na Justiça não é palhaçada", diz Moraes em julgamento de Eduardo
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes stated that 'legal action is not a farce' during the trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro, accusing him of obstruction in the coup plot case and of having full knowledge of his efforts to lobby the Trump administration to pressure the U.S. government against STF ministers and Brazil. Moraes emphasized that the defendant is attempting to evade justice, and the PGR is seeking his conviction for the crime of coercion.

item.title: Michelle e Flávio devem dividir palco no Ceará após disputa interna sobre aliança com Ciro Gomes
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro are set to share the stage at a PL event in Ceará on July 10, following public disagreements over an alliance with Ciro Gomes. Michelle will support the Senate pre-candidacy of Priscila Costa, while Flávio will accompany Alcides Fernandes, highlighting internal divisions over the party’s electoral strategy in the state. Although no explicit endorsements are expected, their joint presence is interpreted by party allies as a symbolic gesture of unity within the Bolsonarist movement.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa cria redes sociais e diz estudar a possibilidade de se lançar à Presidência
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa has created social media profiles and stated he is studying a possible presidential run in 2026. Affiliated with the Christian Democracy party, he met with PSDB leader Aécio Neves to discuss electoral scenarios, though recent polls show only 1% voter intention, concentrated in the Southeast and Central-West regions, with modest appeal among non-Lula and non-Bolsonaro voters.

item.title: Zelensky pede reunião bilateral com Lula no G7
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky requested a bilateral meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France. As of now, the meeting has not been confirmed, though Lula's aides say he is willing to talk, pending schedule alignment. Their last meeting was at the UN General Assembly in September 2025.

item.title: Câmara aprova repúdio a Lula por ligar filhos de Bolsonaro a ‘traidores da Pátria’
item.description: The Chamber's Public Security Committee approved two motions of repudiate against President Lula (PT) over controversial remarks: one for calling Bolsonaro's sons 'traitors of the Fatherland' and another for stating that poor people buy stolen cell phones. The motions, introduced by bolsonarist deputies, were passed with opposition support and triggered judicial reactions, including a lawsuit by Flávio Bolsonaro at the Supreme Court.

item.title: Não é função de deputado fazer 'lobby' no exterior contra o Brasil, diz Moraes em julgamento sobre Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes stated that it is not the function of a Brazilian federal deputy to lobby abroad against Brazil, even with parliamentary immunity, during the trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro for coercion in the course of proceedings. He emphasized that Eduardo failed to notify the Chamber of his change of domicile to the United States and remained abroad to evade justice, stressing that criminal proceedings are not a farce and that legal norms exist to ensure due process and equal defense.

item.title: Vantagem de Lula empolga, mas ordem no governo é ‘humildade para avançar um dia após o outro’
item.description: Lula is gaining ground in voter intention polls against Flávio Bolsonaro, attributed to improved public sentiment and an intensive schedule of government trips delivering projects nationwide. Despite the positive trend, Lula’s team emphasizes humility and steady progress, avoiding overconfidence. Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy has been weakened by controversies involving his ties to Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master, undermining his anti-corruption image in the eyes of Lula’s allies.

item.title: Ao vivo: 1ª Turma do STF analisa denúncia contra Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: The 1st Chamber of the STF is judging this Tuesday (June 16, 2026) the criminal action against former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP), after he failed to present a statement in the case. His defense, conducted by the DPU, requested a postponement, but Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied it, citing the deputy’s disregard for the Court’s decisions. The case is seen as a response to recent international events involving Carla Zambelli and U.S. legal actions tied to Rumble and Trump Media.

item.title: Governo decide sobre aumento do etanol na gasolina em 24 de junho
item.description: The CNPE will decide on June 24 whether to increase ethanol blend in gasoline from 30% to 32% (E32), a measure already announced by President Lula and supported by the MME. The proposal aims to reduce fuel import dependence, with estimated savings of 450 million liters of gasoline annually. The biofuels sector is pushing for approval, which is expected without dissent after two consecutive postponements.

item.title: 1ª Turma do STF julga Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação em processo sobre tentativa de golpe em 2022; ASSISTA
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) is judging Eduardo Bolsonaro for alleged coercion in a case related to the 2022 attempted coup. The Attorney General's Office (PGR) claims he acted under pressure from the U.S. government to block the trial of former President Jair Bolsonaro, while his defense by the Public Defender's Office (DPU) argues freedom of speech and lack of evidence. If convicted, Eduardo Bolsonaro, who currently resides in the United States, could become ineligible to hold public office.

item.title: Pesquisa CNT/MDA: aprovação a Lula supera desaprovação pela primeira vez desde 2024
item.description: The CNT/MDA poll shows President Lula's personal approval rose from 45% to 49%, while disapproval fell from 50% to 46%, marking the first time since November 2024 that he is more approved than disapproved. Government approval also increased from 32% to 35%, with disapproval dropping from 37% to 34%, though both figures remain within the 2.2 percentage point margin of error. The data indicates a modest but meaningful recovery in public perception of the president and his administration.

item.title: STF julga Eduardo Bolsonaro em acusação de coação à Justiça
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) is hearing a criminal case against Eduardo Bolsonaro for allegedly coercing the judiciary by advocating for U.S. sanctions against Brazilian officials, including STF ministers, claiming his father Jair Bolsonaro was politically persecuted. The Public Defender’s Office argues that Justice Alexandre de Moraes should be disqualified due to being targeted by the allegations and that Eduardo’s statements were protected political speech, not illegal coercion.

item.title: Haddad diz que Tarcísio não tem plano para segurança pública
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) for lacking a structured public security plan in São Paulo, stating that the current administration lacks coordination between state and federal forces. He emphasized that combating organized crime requires integration with the Federal Police, Federal Revenue, COAF, and the Public Ministry, citing Operation Carbono Oculto as an example of effective joint action.

item.title: Julgamento de Eduardo amplia guerra de narrativas entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro unfolds amid the intensifying 2026 presidential race, following his and brother Flávio Bolsonaro’s trip to the U.S. and meeting with Donald Trump. U.S. trade measures, including tariffs and the designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, were applied to 59 countries, not exclusively Brazil, according to political scientist Rubens Figueiredo. Nevertheless, the episode poses political risks for Flávio Bolsonaro, as opponents may frame the tariff increases as economically harmful consequences of the Bolsonaro-Trump alignment.
